legend: It is the 25th of January, 2025. You are working on your final report for the statistics class. However, when you enter the calculations into your trusted Brittle Arithmetic Portable Calculator, you notice that the +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ and −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ buttons have malfunctioned. Whenever you press a numeric button (a button from 0$$$\boxed{0}$$$ through 9$$$\boxed{9}$$$ ), an additional button press may be registered immediately after: either the +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ button, or the −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ button, or neither (but never both). "Ugh," you think to yourself, "why did I not buy a Backup Arithmetic Portable Calculator..." But then you get an idea to save yourself from getting a low grade.

After some experimentation, you statistically determined that pressing a numeric button results in an additional +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ input 45%$$$45\%$$$ of the time, and the same holds for the −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ button (and never both at the same time). You decide that you should write your report about your findings. In addition to statistical analysis, the teacher requires you to perform some probabilistic predictions based on a statistical model. You decide to investigate what your calculator does when you try to simply input a natural number.

Given a natural number n$$$n$$$, you consider entering the number into the calculator by pressing the numeric buttons corresponding to the standard base 10$$$10$$$ representation of n$$$n$$$. The calculator may register a +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ or −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ button press in between the digits of n$$$n$$$, which results in an arithmetic expression. You wonder what happens if you press =$$$\boxed{=}$$$ to evaluate the expression. Luckily, if your expression ends with a +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ or −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ , the calculator ignores this, such that this evaluation always results in an integer. To finish your report, you decide to write a program that determines the expected value of this result for any given value of n$$$n$$$.
input: One line with an integer n$$$n$$$ (0≤n<101000$$$0 \leq n  \lt  10^{1000}$$$), the number that you will enter into the calculator.
output: Output the expected value of the result.
Your answer should have an absolute or relative error of at most 10−6$$$10^{-6}$$$.

legend.ai: 现在是 2025 年 1 月 25 日。你正在为统计课撰写期末报告。然而，当你将计算式输入你信赖的 Brittle Arithmetic Portable Calculator 时，你发现 +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ 和 −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ 按钮出现了故障。每当你按下一个数字按钮(从 0$$$\boxed{0}$$$ 到 9$$$\boxed{9}$$$  的按钮)时，紧接着可能会额外记录一次按钮按下操作：要么是 +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ 按钮，要么是 −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ 按钮，要么什么都没有(但绝不会两者同时出现)。“唉，”你心想，“我当初为什么没买一台备用的 Backup Arithmetic Portable Calculator……”但随后你想到了一个办法，可以避免自己拿到低分。
经过一些实验，你通过统计确定，按下数字按钮后，有 45%$$$45\%$$$ 的概率会额外输入 +$$$\boxed{+}$$$，−$$$\boxed{-}$$$ 按钮也是如此(并且绝不会同时出现两者)。你决定将你的发现写进报告。除了统计分析外，老师还要求你基于统计模型进行一些概率预测。你决定研究当你尝试直接输入一个自然数时，计算器会做什么。

给定一个自然数 n$$$n$$$，你考虑通过按下与 n$$$n$$$ 的标准十进制$$$10$$$ 表示对应的数字按钮，将这个数输入计算器。在 n$$$n$$$ 的各个数字之间，计算器可能会记录一次 +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ 或 −$$$\boxed{-}$$$ 按钮按下操作，从而形成一个算术表达式。你想知道按下 =$$$\boxed{=}$$$ 计算该表达式会发生什么。幸运的是，如果表达式以 +$$$\boxed{+}$$$ 或 −$$$\boxed{-}$$$  结尾，计算器会忽略末尾的运算符，因此计算结果总是一个整数。为了完成报告，你决定编写一个程序，求出给定任意 n$$$n$$$ 时该结果的期望值。

input.ai: 一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(0≤n<101000$$$0 \leq n  \lt  10^{1000}$$$)，表示你将输入计算器的数。

output.ai: 你的答案的绝对误差或相对误差应不超过 10−6$$$10^{-6}$$$。
